messages.subject: News about attributes
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

As all of you probably know, arrival attributes can be retrieved by defining functions with one argument. A very simple example:
traj <- trajectory() %>%
  set_attribute("delay", 3) %>%
  timeout(function(attr) attr["delay"])

Then we implemented support for global attributes, making it necessary to add a second argument to retrieve this new set of attributes:
traj <- trajectory() %>%
  set_attribute("delay", 3, global=TRUE) %>%
  timeout(function(attr, glb) glb["delay"])

This method is a kind of rarity. It’s clunky, as it is not easy to document (and therefore to discover and learn), and non-scalable, because new features would require more and more additional arguments. Thus, it will be deprecated starting at version 3.6.3, which will be released at the end of this month.

The new official method for retrieving attributes will be get_attribute(). It works in the same way as now() for the simulation time:
env <- simmer()

traj <- trajectory() %>%
  set_attribute("delay", 3) %>%
  timeout(function() get_attribute(env, "delay"))

and for global attributes:
env <- simmer()

traj <- trajectory() %>%
  set_attribute("delay", 3, global=TRUE) %>%
  timeout(function() get_attribute(env, "delay", global=TRUE))

This is a little bit more verbose, but I believe it’s more consistent and intuitive. Moreover, it allows us to easily implement new features for extracting arrival information. In fact, get_attribute() will come hand in hand with two more verbs: get_name() and get_prioritization(), to retrieve the arrival name and prioritization values respectively.

The old method will be still available throughout the 3.6.x series, showing a warning from 3.6.3 on, and will be removed in version 3.7.

Regards,
Iñaki
